passages.text: This is the burden against Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor. Word has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
passages.sermon:
This message is a prophecy against Tyre.
Tyre was a powerful city.
God declares judgment against Tyre.
Ships from Tarshish traveled far for trade.
God tells the ships of Tarshish to wail.
Tyre is destroyed.
Tyre has no house left.
Tyre has no harbor left.
People in Cyprus have heard the news.
The news of Tyre’s destruction has reached them.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ׀ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־ שֻׁדַּ֤ד מִבַּ֙יִת֙ מִבּ֔וֹא מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כִּתִּ֖ים נִגְלָה־ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Be silent, O dwellers of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, whose traders have crossed the sea.
passages.sermon: The people who live on the coast must be silent.\r\nThe merchants of Sidon must be silent.\r\nThe traders from Sidon have crossed the sea.
passages.original: דֹּ֖מּוּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אִ֑י סֹחֵ֥ר צִיד֛וֹן עֹבֵ֥ר יָ֖ם מִלְאֽוּךְ׃

passages.text: On the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre; she was the merchant of the nations.
passages.sermon:
Tyre was a powerful city.
Tyre traded with many nations.
Ships brought grain from Shihor on the great waters to Tyre.
The harvest of the Nile became Tyre’s wealth.
Tyre gained her income from this trade.
Tyre acted as the merchant for many nations.
passages.original: וּבְמַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ זֶ֣רַע שִׁחֹ֔ר קְצִ֥יר יְא֖וֹר תְּבֽוּאָתָ֑הּ וַתְּהִ֖י סְחַ֥ר גּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: Be ashamed, O Sidon, the stronghold of the sea, for the sea has spoken: “I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
passages.sermon:
Sidon is a city.
Sidon is a stronghold by the sea.
Sidon, be ashamed.
The sea has spoken.
The sea says, "I have not been in labor."
The sea says, "I have not given birth."
The sea says, "I have not raised young men."
The sea says, "I have not brought up young women."
passages.original: בּ֣וֹשִׁי צִיד֔וֹן כִּֽי־ אָמַ֣ר יָ֔ם מָע֥וֹז הַיָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־ חַ֣לְתִּי וְלֹֽא־ יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְלֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe in agony over the news of Tyre.
passages.sermon: Egypt will hear a report about Tyre.\r\nThe people of Egypt will feel great pain.\r\nThey will suffer when they hear the news about Tyre.
passages.original: כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ שֵׁ֖מַע לְמִצְרָ֑יִם יָחִ֖ילוּ כְּשֵׁ֥מַע צֹֽר׃

passages.text: Cross over to Tarshish; wail, O inhabitants of the coastland!
passages.sermon: The prophet Isaiah speaks to the people living on the coastland.\r\nHe tells them to cross over to Tarshish.\r\nHe commands the inhabitants of the coastland to wail.

passages.text: Is this your jubilant city, whose origin is from antiquity, whose feet have taken her to settle far away?
passages.sermon:
Tyre is a city.
Tyre was once joyful.
Tyre existed since ancient times.
Tyre’s people traveled far away.
Tyre’s people went to live in distant places.
passages.original: הֲזֹ֥את לָכֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽימֵי־ קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָהּ֙ יֹבִל֣וּהָ רַגְלֶ֔יהָ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לָגֽוּר׃

passages.text: Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose traders are princes, whose merchants are renowned on the earth?
passages.sermon:
Tyre is a city.
Tyre gives crowns to others.
Tyre’s traders are princes.
Tyre’s merchants are famous on the earth.
Who planned this against Tyre?
passages.original: מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל־ צֹ֖ר הַמַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֙יה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖יהָ נִכְבַּדֵּי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts planned it, to defile all its glorious beauty, to disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
passages.sermon: The LORD of Hosts made a plan.\r\nHe decided to defile all glorious beauty.\r\nHe chose to disgrace all the renowned people of the earth.
passages.original: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יְעָצָ֑הּ לְחַלֵּל֙ גְּא֣וֹן כָּל־ צְבִ֔י לְהָקֵ֖ל כָּל־ נִכְבַּדֵּי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Cultivate your land like the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer a harbor.
passages.sermon:
O Daughter of Tarshish, you are a people who once had a harbor.
Now you have no harbor.
Work your land as the Egyptians work the land by the Nile.
You must now depend on your land, not on the sea.
passages.original: עִבְרִ֥י אַרְצֵ֖ךְ כַּיְאֹ֑ר בַּת־ תַּרְשִׁ֕ישׁ אֵ֖ין מֵ֥זַח עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: The LORD has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has made kingdoms tremble. He has given a command that the strongholds of Canaan be destroyed.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the LORD of Hosts.
The LORD stretched out His hand over the sea.
The LORD made kingdoms tremble.
The LORD gave a command against Canaan.
The LORD ordered the destruction of Canaan’s strongholds.
passages.original: יָדוֹ֙ נָטָ֣ה עַל־ הַיָּ֔ם הִרְגִּ֖יז מַמְלָכ֑וֹת יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶל־ כְּנַ֔עַן לַשְׁמִ֖ד מָעֻזְנֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: He said, “You shall rejoice no more, O oppressed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Cyprus— even there you will find no rest.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to the people of Sidon.
Sidon is called the oppressed Virgin Daughter.
He said, “You will not rejoice anymore.
You are suffering.
Get up.
Go over to the land of the Kittim, which is Cyprus.
Even in Cyprus, you will not find rest.
You will not have peace anywhere.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־ תוֹסִ֥יפִי ע֖וֹד לַעְל֑וֹז הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָ֞ה בְּתוּלַ֣ת בַּת־ צִיד֗וֹן כִּתִּיִּים ק֣וּמִי עֲבֹ֔רִי גַּם־ שָׁ֖ם לֹא־ יָנ֥וּחַֽ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Look at the land of the Chaldeans — a people now of no account. The Assyrians destined it for the desert creatures; they set up their siege towers and stripped its palaces. They brought it to ruin.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans once lived in this land.
Now, the Chaldeans are nothing.
The Assyrians took this land.
The Assyrians planned for wild animals to live here.
The Assyrians built siege towers against the city.
They destroyed the palaces.
They made the land a ruin.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן׀ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣הּ לְצִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ בְחִינָיו עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שָׂמָ֖הּ לְמַפֵּלָֽה׃

passages.text: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your harbor has been destroyed!
passages.sermon:
The ships of Tarshish are large trading vessels.
These ships travel far across the sea.
The harbor is a place where ships find safety and trade goods.
The harbor has been destroyed.
The ships of Tarshish must wail.
They have lost their safe place.
They have lost their place of trade.
passages.original: הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מָעֻזְּכֶֽן׃ס

passages.text: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years—the span of a king’s life. But at the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the harlot: “Take up your harp, stroll through the city, O forgotten harlot. Make sweet melody, sing many a song, so you will be remembered.”
passages.sermon:
Tyre was a powerful and wealthy city.
God said Tyre would be forgotten.
This would last for seventy years.
Seventy years is the length of a king’s life.
After seventy years, Tyre would be remembered again.
Tyre would be like a harlot in a song.
The song says, “Take your harp.
Walk through the city, forgotten harlot.
Play your music well.
Sing many songs.
Do this so people will remember you.”
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה׃ קְחִ֥י כִנּ֛וֹר סֹ֥בִּי עִ֖יר זוֹנָ֣ה נִשְׁכָּחָ֑ה הֵיטִ֤יבִי נַגֵּן֙ הַרְבִּי־ שִׁ֔יר לְמַ֖עַן תִּזָּכֵֽרִי׃

passages.text: And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will restore Tyre. Then she will return to hire as a prostitute and sell herself to all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will act after seventy years.
The LORD will visit Tyre.
Tyre is a city.
Tyre will return to her former trade.
Tyre will act like a prostitute.
Tyre will offer herself to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Tyre will do this before all the nations on the face of the earth.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֞ה מִקֵּ֣ץ׀ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יִפְקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ צֹ֔ר וְשָׁבָ֖ה לְאֶתְנַנָּ֑ה וְזָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת־ כָּל־ מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Yet her profits and wages will be set apart to the LORD; they will not be stored or saved, for her profit will go to those who live before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.
passages.sermon:
Tyre is a city.
Tyre will have profits and wages.
These profits and wages will be set apart for the LORD.
No one will store these profits.
No one will save these profits.
People who live before the LORD will receive Tyre’s profits.
They will use the profits for abundant food.
They will use the profits for fine clothing.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה סַחְרָ֜הּ וְאֶתְנַנָּ֗הּ קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵֽאָצֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יֵֽחָסֵ֑ן כִּ֣י לַיֹּשְׁבִ֞ים לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה סַחְרָ֔הּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְשָׂבְעָ֖ה וְלִמְכַסֶּ֥ה עָתִֽיק׃פ
